source.title: Automatic Image-Level Morphological Trait Annotation for Organismal Images
source.authors: Vardaan Pahuja; Samuel Stevens; Alyson East; S. Record; Yu Su

record.tranche_reason: The study qualitatively examines whether selected SAE latent units in a vision representation align with coherent visual parts, using neuron-activation analysis rather than the original studies' methods. It does not assess the prevalence of polysemantic neurons across a model.
record.gate_note: The paper reports selected SAE latent examples that activate on particular insect parts. These bear on feature coherence, but the study does not systematically test unrelated inputs or quantify how often units are polysemantic. Its rating, classification, and runtime results concern the annotation pipeline rather than polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE latents over DINOv2-base features as part detectors for a trait-annotation pipeline and mainly reports pipeline quality: ratings, classification and cost. Its neuron analysis covers a few hand-picked SAE dictionary latents, not the backbone's own neurons. It never measures whether model neurons are polysemantic, what causes it, or how often it occurs. No version (V1–V7) is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs on DINOv2 features yield monosemantic, spatially grounded latents usable as part detectors. They show the resulting pipeline (BIOSCAN-Traits) gives better-rated trait descriptions than an MLLM-only baseline and improves BioCLIP zero-shot classification. They acknowledge some latents may encode co-occurring traits and do not treat SAE features as true traits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a ReLU SAE over DINOv2-base image features and inspects selected spatial activations for insect morphology; it does not reproduce the original neuron analysis or test canonical mixed-activation examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Annotation quality changes with SAE sparsity, trait-frequency threshold, number of images per prompt, and MLLM choice; these ablations do not measure changes in polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected top-activating latents of a ReLU SAE (24,576 latents) on DINOv2-base features each localize to a single insect part (wings, antennae, thorax, leg junction, eyes, abdomen). The authors note some latents may capture multiple co-occurring traits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse autoencoder latents trained on vision foundation-model features yield spatially coherent, largely monosemantic part detectors.

record.problems: Neuron evidence consists of selected qualitative examples, with no systematic estimate of how many units are coherent or polysemantic and no test against unrelated inputs. The authors note that there are no ground-truth morphological trait annotations at scale and that some latents may represent multiple co-occurring traits.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear directly on the tested feature-coherence question. The paper's human-rating and downstream-classification results evaluate trait annotation and model utility, not neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No analysis of the image classifier's own neurons or responses to unrelated inputs.
No test of superposition as a cause.
No test of non-capacity sources of polysemanticity.
The SAE sparsity ablation measures annotation ratings, not the share of polysemantic neurons.
No canonical polysemantic neurons are re-examined; the SAE latent examples are selected and unquantified.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is removed. SAE latents are a learned dictionary, not the model's neurons, and the examples are cherry-picked top-activating units with no prevalence estimate. The paper's monosemanticity claim is asserted from examples rather than tested. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test ordinary image-classifier neurons such as InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 or responses to unrelated input categories.
No transformer language-model MLP neurons or language inputs are studied.
Does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Does not test polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.

The paper varies SAE sparsity and other annotation-pipeline choices, but does not measure how architecture or training choices change the share of polysemantic neurons or the performance cost of reducing that share.
Examines selected SAE latent units in insect images, not canonical polysemantic neurons or the prevalence of unrelated mixtures across all units.
Does not compare activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for deciding whether a neuron is polysemantic.
